props.gloss_en: the mishnah: over vegetables one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
over boiled vegetables one blesses 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
over boiled vegetables one blesses 'By whose word all things came to be'
Rav Chisda: whatever is 'fruit of the ground' at first [raw], once boiled -- 'By whose word'
Rav Chisda: whatever is 'By whose word' at first, once boiled -- 'fruit of the ground'
the second clause (שהכל raw, האדמה boiled) is found in cabbage, beet and pumpkin
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the first clause (האדמה raw, שהכל boiled) is found in garlic and leeks
Rav Nachman: the dispute over boiled vegetables is taught as a [tannaitic] dispute -- R' Meir and R' Yosei on boiled matza
R' Meir: one fulfils [the matza obligation] with a soaked wafer and with a boiled one that has not dissolved
R' Yosei: with a soaked wafer one fulfils, but not with a boiled one, even if it has not dissolved
R' Yosei said it there only because we require the taste of matza, and it is lacking
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: Ulla fixed his error according to R' Binyamin bar Yefet
R' Zeira: R' Binyamin bar Yefet is not to be set beside R' Chiyya bar Abba -- the latter's tradition of R' Yochanan outweighs his
R' Chiyya bar Abba was exact in learning the teaching from R' Yochanan his master; R' Binyamin bar Yefet was not
moreover, R' Chiyya bar Abba reviewed his learning before R' Yochanan every thirty days; R' Binyamin bar Yefet did not
R' Yochanan, asked about the lupin boiled seven times in a pot and eaten at the end of the meal: one blesses over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
R' Chiyya bar Abba: I saw R' Yochanan eat a salted olive and bless over it before and after
the baraita: the vegetables with which one fulfils [maror] on Pesach -- he fulfils with them and their stalks, but not pickled, not boiled, not cooked
R' Zeira: we do not require a large olive[-bulk]; we require a medium one
and the olive brought before R' Yochanan was a large one, so even with its pit removed the measure remained
the mishnah: the olive they spoke of is neither small nor large but medium -- the aguri
R' Abbahu: its name is not aguri but avruti
and some say [R' Abbahu said]: its name is samrusi
and why is it called aguri? because its oil is stored within it
cabbage, Damascene plums and pullets were brought before bar Kappara; the student he permitted to bless hurried and blessed over the pullets, and his fellow mocked him
bar Kappara: not at the blesser am I angry but at the mocker -- if your fellow is like one who never tasted meat, why did you mock him?
bar Kappara, again: not at the mocker am I angry but at the blesser -- if there is no wisdom here, is there no elder here?
and neither of them lived out his year
(entertained) the dispute over boiled vegetables is the dispute of bar Kappara's two students
over pullets one blesses 'By whose word all things came to be'
the food one prefers takes precedence [for the first blessing]
the fruit [whose blessing is האדמה] takes precedence
the cabbage takes precedence
[cabbage takes precedence] because it nourishes
turnip heads cut into large pieces -- 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
[turnip heads] cut small -- 'By whose word all things came to be'
Rav Yehuda: both these and those -- 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
and cutting them small is done only to sweeten the taste
a cooked dish of beets, to which they add little flour -- 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
[a cooked dish] of turnips, to which they add more flour -- 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
and he said again: both these and those -- 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
and the extra flour thrown in is only to make it bind
Rav Chisda: a cooked dish of beets is good for the heart and good for the eyes, and all the more for the bowels
Abaye: that is when it sits on the stove and goes 'tukh tukh'
Rav Pappa: beet-water is as beets
and turnip-water is as turnips
and the water of all boiled things is as those boiled things
dill, once it has given its flavour in the pot, is no longer subject to teruma and does not contract food-impurity
learn from it: dill is put in [the pot] to sweeten the taste
Rav Chiyya bar Ashi: over dry bread soaked in a bowl one blesses 'Who brings forth bread'
R' Chiyya: the blessing must end together with the bread
the stam: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi's ruling disagrees with R' Chiyya's -- on R' Chiyya's rule soaked bread would not get 'Who brings forth'
Rava: one blesses and afterwards breaks
the Nehardeans act according to R' Chiyya
and the Rabbis act according to Rava
Ravina: my mother told me -- your father acted according to R' Chiyya

supports.gloss_en: קתני ירקות דומיא דפת: מה פת שנשתנה על ידי האור, אף ירקות נמי שנשתנו על ידי האור -- ממאי? מדקתני ירקות דומיא דפת
דתניא: soaked wafer and boiled-undissolved matza -- R' Meir: fulfils; R' Yosei: not the boiled one. The marker is a bare דתניא (no SupportKind names it)
ועוד, בר מן דין ובר מן דין: the lupin boiled seven times -- R' Yochanan ruled בורא פרי האדמה
אי אמרת בשלמא שלקות במילתייהו קיימי -- before העץ, after מעין שלש; אלא אי אמרת לאו במילתייהו קיימי -- before שהכל, but after, what does he bless? so R' Yochanan held boiled things stay in their state

deflected_by.gloss_en: דילמא בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן -- perhaps after [a שהכל food] he blessed 'Who creates many living things', so the practice proves nothing

supports.gloss_en: דתנן: זית שאמרו לא קטן ולא גדול אלא בינוני -- the mishnah's olive-measure is the medium olive. The marker is a bare דתנן (no SupportKind names it)
תא שמע: השבת משנתנה טעם בקדירה אין בה משום תרומה -- once its flavour is given it is spent, so it was put in for flavour; שמע מינה

objections.gloss_en: בשלמא כל שתחילתו שהכל שלקו האדמה -- משכחת לה בכרבא וסלקא וקרא; אלא כל שתחילתו האדמה שלקו שהכל -- היכי משכחת לה? -- where is there any vegetable of Rav Chisda's first kind?

answered_by.gloss_en: משכחת לה בתומי וכרתי -- garlic and leeks (= p_mashkachat_tumei_vecharatei)

objections.gloss_en: ולא היא: דכולי עלמא שלקות בורא פרי האדמה; R' Yosei disqualified boiled matza only because the taste of matza is required, and here even he agrees -- the tannaitic dispute is not this one
the baraita disqualifies boiled vegetables for maror; ואי סלקא דעתך במילתייהו קאי -- שלוקין אמאי לא? if boiled vegetables stay in their state [the premise of האדמה], why are they unfit?

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני התם דבעינן טעם מרור וליכא -- there the taste of maror is required and it is lacking; that says nothing about their state

objections.gloss_en: רבי יוחנן היכי מברך על זית מליח? כיון דשקילא לגרעיניה בצר ליה שיעורא -- with its pit removed the olive lacks the measure, so how could R' Yochanan bless after it?

answered_by.gloss_en: מי סברת כזית גדול בעינן? כזית בינוני בעינן, וההוא זית גדול הוה -- the measure is a medium olive, and that olive was large, so pitted it still sufficed (= p_kezayit_beinoni, p_zayit_gadol_hava)

objections.gloss_en: מאי שנא צנומה דלא, משום דכי כליא ברכה אפרוסה קא כליא? על הפת נמי, כי קא גמרה -- אפרוסה גמרה! -- whole bread too ends its blessing on a slice, so R' Chiyya's rule cannot be what denies soaked bread המוציא

rulings.gloss_en: והלכתא כרבא, דאמר מברך ואחר כך בוצע
